title: President Biden announces a three-phase Israeli ceasefire proposal for Gaza
body:
On 31 May 2024, United States President Joe Biden gave a speech at the White House setting out a three-phase proposal that he described as an Israeli plan for a ceasefire in Gaza and the release of hostages. He called it a road map to an enduring ceasefire and the release of all hostages and urged Hamas to accept it, arguing that Hamas no longer had the capability to carry out an attack like that of 7 October 2023.

The first phase would last six weeks and include a full ceasefire, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from all populated areas of Gaza, and the release of some hostages in exchange for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners. In the second phase, negotiations would continue and, in Biden's account, could lead to a permanent end to hostilities and the release of all remaining living hostages. The third phase would be reconstruction of Gaza.

Hamas had not agreed to the plan and had said it would not accept a deal that did not guarantee a permanent ceasefire, although a Hamas statement said it viewed the speech positively. Biden acknowledged that some members of the Israeli government might not support the deal, and Netanyahu's office said Israel would keep fighting until its war aims were achieved. Biden faced criticism within his own party over civilian casualties in Gaza.
